newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian rights activist misses Oslo visit.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian rights activist misses Oslo visit.

text.p: A leading Palestinian human rights activist said on Monday Palestinian officials told him he had been banned by Israel from travelling to Norway for a conference on "Citizenship and the State in the Middle East".

But a spokesman for Israel's civil administration in Gaza denied any Israeli travel restrictions had been imposed on Iyad al-Sarraj, director of the Palestinian Commission for Citizen's Rights and the Gaza Mental Health Programme.

Under Israeli-PLO peace deals, Israel maintains overall control of borders in Gaza and the West Bank and the Palestinian Authority submits travel requests to Israel on behalf of Arabs in the self-ruled areas.
Sarraj had said "Israeli Security", citing "security reasons" had told him he could not travel to Oslo for Monday's conference.
But he later said in a telephone interview with Reuters that Israel's purported decision had been told to him by Palestinian officials and he had not spoken to Israeli authorities.

"I tried to call (Israel's) Arab affairs officer...but he was not available...I called the (Palestinian) Authority and told (an official) and he came back to me and said he couldn't reach any Israeli officer," Sarraj said.
Sarraj was jailed twice this year by the Palestinian Authority in Gaza on defamation charges -- later dropped -- after he attacked its human rights record in a New York Times interview.

"I do not see any (travel) request for Sarraj from the Palestinian Authority," said Lieutenant Avi Gambash, Israel's civil administration spokesman in Gaza. He said he had checked computer records and with the relevant Israeli officials.
"As far as I know we have no security problem with Sarraj or any problem with giving him a permit," Gambash said.
